9. In the present case, the injured /petitioner has specifically deposed about accident by stating that the accident occurred due to sudden and negligent opening of the left door of the offending vehicle by Respondent no.2.

During cross- examination of PW-1 it was admitted that the offending vehicle was in a stationery position at the time of the accident and that the petitioner was trying to cross (overtake) the same from its left side.

Whether the driver of the offending vehicle, Respondent no.1 or Respondent no.2 i.e. co-passenger in the offending vehicle were rash or negligent has to be decided on the basis of the facts and circumstances.

The site plan of the incident shows the accident to have occurred a few meters from the red light located in the center of a crossing (leading to 4 different roads) while the road on which the accident took place apparently had a free left
Thus, based on the site plan, petitioner cannot be said to have been negligent in plying his motorcycle on the left side of such road, for taking a left turn.

At the same time even if the offending vehicle was at halt due to the red light, it is impermissible for any such halting vehicle to deboard any MACT No. 37/2017 K. Suresh vs. Agnibh Mudi & ors. Page no. 6 of 22 ss passenger sitting therein

A vehicle halted due to red light cannot be equated with a vehicle parked on the side of the road and as such, the level of precaution expected from the vehicle at halt due to the red light is much more than a vehicle parked on the extreme
The site plan clearly shows that the offending vehicle was not parked on the extreme side of the road nor was there any indicator or parking lights of such vehicle switched on.
No person plying on the road could have reasonably expected that the door of such halted vehicle would suddenly open.
The driver of the offending vehicle was certainly at fault in halting the vehicle in defiance of the traffic signal and for deboarding its passenger.
In fact the offending vehicle is VXI model of Swift Car which is enabled with an automatic locking system of the doors of the car once the car starts plying on the road at a minimum speed.
After the doors of the car are automatically locked, the same can only be opened either by the driver of the car from the centralized locking system of the car or manually, by the passenger.

Respondent no. 1 has nowhere taken a defence or pleaded that Respondent no.2 had opened the lock of the door without his knowledge and as such it is presumed that Respondent no.2 was deboarding the offending vehicle with consent or atleast

10. By entering into the witness box, Respondent no.1 has testified as R1W1 that he had rightfully stopped his car at a temporary auto stand and a semi circular area de-marketed for auto stand or halting of any moving vehicle.
He has simultaneously asserted that he had halted his car 100 meters away from the red light to enable his friend /Respondent no.2 to alight.
There is however no indication in the site plan nor any proof of any auto stand being at the spot of accident, filed by Respondent no.1.
Contrary stand taken by R1W1 with regard to halting of his vehicle either at the red light or at an alleged 'temporary' auto stand renders his defence unreliable.
However, mere non registration of a criminal case against Respondent no.1, would not exonerate him of his liability under the Motor Vehicle Act.
